messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy@brightlinehealth.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Annual commit review — capacity mapping & QBR scheduling

Hi Ivy / Carlos,

Hope you’re both well. As we approach the anniversary of your committed capacity, I wanted to propose a short cadence to align on the next 12 months: review current consumption patterns, confirm any headroom you need, and lock in a QBR to cover operational and commercial items.

High-level proposal:
- Week of Jun 21: internal usage runbook + ops deep-dive (we share a usage extract)
- Jun 28–30: scheduled QBR (30–45m) including stakeholders below
- Early Jul: finalize any contract amendment / SOW updates + timeline

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Confirm whether you expect a committed increase of tokens, or prefer an overage plan for the next 3–6 months.
2) Share any new business lines or pilots launching H2 that will materially change throughput.
3) Please propose 2x 30–45m windows for a QBR — we’ll lock one.

I’ve attached a proposed QBR agenda and pulled the May usage snapshot for your review (see attachments). Vanessa will own the capacity mapping; Marcus will draft the SOW language if there’s a scope change.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0182

Attachments: BRIGHTLINE_SOW_v2.pdf (draft), usage_report_May2027.csv (summary), QBR_agenda.docx
From: Ivy Chen <ivy@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annual commit review — capacity mapping & QBR scheduling

Thanks Hannah — this is great.

Quick answers:
- We’re seeing steady growth from two pilot programs; likely need +30–40% committed capacity by Sep if both convert.
- Prefer a committed increase rather than consistent overage; budgeting is clearer for us.
- QBR availability: Jun 29 (10:00–10:45 PT) or Jul 1 (14:00–14:45 PT) — either works.

Can you share any sample SOW language for the capacity uplift and whether there’s a short-term uplift option (90-day ramp) vs annual commit? Also we’ll want to review pricing tiers.

Appreciate the agenda and usage file — Carlos and I will take a look and get back with specifics.

—Ivy
Ivy Chen
Head of Data & AI, Brightline Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Annual commit review — capacity mapping & QBR scheduling

Team — forwarding Ivy’s reply. Quick alignment notes:
- Ivy requests +30–40% committed by Sep; they prefer an annual commit but asked about 90-day ramp option.
- They picked Jun 29 10:00 PT as preferred QBR slot (tentative).

Action items:
- Vanessa: can you produce a capacity mapping run (tokens/day, p95 latency impact, estimated cost delta) by Wed EOD? Use the May extract as baseline.
- Marcus: please prepare two SOW options — (A) annual commit + tiered pricing and (B) 90-day provisional uplift with checkpoint. Draft language and highlight approval paths.
- Neha: will you own discount approvals and comping guidelines? If so, we need an internal stub for what level of discount we can offer for a +30–40% commit.

I’ll schedule the Jun 29 QBR as tentative and include the agenda. If pricing needs legal or finance, I’ll loop them before the meeting.

Thanks — Hannah

All — I sketched two SOW drafts and attached a short commercial note. Key points:
- Option A (Annual commit): +35% tokens, 12-month term, 10% volume discount on incremental usage over baseline.
- Option B (90-day uplift): +40% provisional for 90 days with a checkpoint. If consumption sustains, convert to Option A with prorated billing.

I’ve included redline notes where finance/legal signoff will be required (pricing floor and SLA changes). I can convert to a formal SOW doc if we agree on a path.

I’ll also prepare a usage sensitivity table so we can show Brightline five scenarios (base / +20 / +35 / +50 / spike).

Marcus
